steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: An operational amplifier (op-amp) is a high-gain differential amplifier with two inputs: inverting (−) and non-inverting (+).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The ideal op-amp has infinite open-loop gain, infinite input impedance, zero output impedance and infinite bandwidth.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A real op-amp has very high but finite open-loop gain (typically 10⁵ to 10⁶), high input impedance and low output impedance.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Negative feedback is used to control gain and improve stability; it reduces overall gain to a predictable value set by external components.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: An inverting amplifier has Rin = 10 kΩ and Rf = 100 kΩ. What is its voltage gain? | Q: A non-inverting amplifier has Rf = 47 kΩ and R1 = 10 kΩ. Calculate the voltage gain. | Q: State two properties of an ideal op-amp.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Av = −Rf/Rin = −100/10 = −10. The gain magnitude is 10 and the output is inverted. | Av = 1 + Rf/R1 = 1 + 47/10 = 1 + 4.7 = 5.7. | Infinite open-loop gain and infinite input impedance (also zero output impedance and infinite bandwidth).

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always show the formula before substituting values: Av = −Rf/Rin for inverting, Av = 1 + Rf/R1 for non-inverting. Remember the minus sign for inverting amplifier gain — the output is phase-inverted. When asked about ideal op-amp properties, list at least two: infinite gain, infinite input impedance, zero output impedance. Draw the op-amp circuit diagram with correct input labels: (−) for inverting, (+) for non-inverting. State the virtual earth principle when explaining how an inverting amplifier works.
